ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black/dark grey) pixels account for approximately 92% of the surface area, with high-intensity (white) pixels forming localized clusters accounting for approximately 8% of the visible surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Solid black base. High-contrast white mottling concentrated at the trailing edge tips and along the upper border of both lobes. Significant white pixel clustering is visible on the distal ends of the trailing edge.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Shallow V-shaped depression with an approximate pixel angle of 140 degrees and a narrow depth relative to the total fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Highly irregular trailing edge characterized by high-frequency, low-amplitude serrations (peaks and valleys of 5-15 pixels) across the entire boundary, with larger indentations visible on the outer lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Bi-lateral concave sweep trajectory from the median notch extending toward the distal tips, terminating in jagged, irregular points.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Multiple circular high-contrast pixel clusters (rosettes) distributed across the dark surface, with a notable concentration of three circular marks on the mid-right lobe and several smaller ones on the left lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several distinct linear disruptions: a prominent horizontal white scratch in the center of the left lobe and multiple short, unaligned vertical scratches on the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive irregular edge morphology suggesting historical tissue loss or mechanical wear; scattered white pitting across the ventral surface representing healed parasitic or barnacle attachment sites.
other_distinctive_markers: A distinctive vertical chain of small, white high-intensity pixels following the longitudinal ridge from the peduncle base toward the median notch.
